section_summary: This section covers diplomatic and interdepartmental records from January 1930 to May 1931 concerning radio frequency interference between Japanese wireless stations and United States naval and amateur stations. A primary focus is resolving mutual interference between the Japanese Wireless Telegraph Company station JAA at Iwaki and U.S. Naval station NPO at Cavite, leading to Japan shifting Iwaki's operating frequency and discontinuing its obsolete arc transmitter. The section also documents naval complaints regarding Choshi station JCS interfering with naval press reception in Samoa, as well as extensive formal complaints from the American Radio Relay League and Federal Radio Commission regarding numerous Japanese commercial and government stations operating illegally within international amateur bands.

subfiles.summary: The American Radio Relay League presents detailed evidence of severe interference caused to amateur communications by Japanese non-amateur stations operating within the exclusive 7,000–7,300 kilocycle band in violation of the 1927 Washington Convention.
